question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the second term using the definition of $\operatorname{tan}⁡x.$ This gives:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}+\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}
$$

Next, we put both terms over a common denominator, and combine the two fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)} \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)} & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+({cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}+\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\operatorname{sec}⁡x.
$$
